description: Parity tracking for @cueapi/mcp against the hosted CueAPI API. Enumerates which API surfaces this MCP server exposes as tools and which it doesn't, so drift becomes visible at audit time. Per the 3-layer parity discipline (PR template + this manifest + Backlog rows for each port).
audit_methodology: Walk every endpoint in private cueapi/app/routers/ and check coverage in src/tools.ts. For each covered tool, walk the corresponding schemas/*.py to verify field-level coverage in the tool's zod input schema + the response shape it surfaces. Drift goes in `endpoints_missing` or `tool_param_drift` keyed by tool name.
audit_cadence: Monthly full sweep. Per-PR diffs handled via the .github/pull_request_template.md `Parity Impact` section in the private repo.

PATCH /v1/cues/{id}.tool: cueapi_update_cue, cueapi_pause_cue, cueapi_resume_cue (pause/resume are PATCH variants with status field, not separate endpoints)

POST /v1/executions/{id}/claim.tool: cueapi_claim_execution AND cueapi_claim_next_execution (the latter discovers exec_id via /claimable then claims by id; does NOT use the dedicated POST /v1/executions/claim route — see open_implementation_drift below)

POST /v1/auth/register.blocker: Account creation is out of scope for an MCP server; users register via web/CLI.

GET /v1/auth/me.blocker: MCP tooling validates the API key implicitly via every call's 401 surface; a dedicated whoami tool is low-value. Could add for parity if other agents request it.

POST /v1/device-codes.blocker: Device-code OAuth flow is CLI-only (cueapi-cli auth).

POST /v1/auth/key/regenerate.blocker: Risky destructive op; intentionally not surfaced. Re-evaluate if MCP-driven workflow needs it.

GET /v1/auth/webhook-secret.blocker: Webhook-secret retrieval — agents running their own webhook servers may want this. Re-evaluate.

POST /v1/executions/{id}/replay.blocker: Used for retry-from-failure flows; not yet wrapped. Worth adding for symmetry with claim/heartbeat surface.

POST /v1/executions/{id}/verification-pe.blocker: Verification-state transition; not yet wrapped. Pairs with the verify endpoint below.

POST /v1/executions/{id}/verify.blocker: Mark execution verified — not yet wrapped.

PATCH /v1/executions/{id}/evidence.blocker: Update execution evidence (external_id, result_url, summary, etc.). Not yet wrapped — useful for agents that report verification asynchronously.

POST /v1/executions/claim.blocker: Dedicated claim-next route (atomic discover+claim in single call). Today cueapi_claim_next_execution wraps this conceptually but implements via /claimable + /{id}/claim two-step. Worth migrating to the dedicated route to avoid the race window between discover and claim.

POST /v1/worker/heartbeat.blocker: Worker-level heartbeat is for the cueapi-worker daemon, not user-facing MCP tooling. Per-execution heartbeat (cueapi_execution_heartbeat) is the relevant surface for MCP consumers.

GET /v1/workers.blocker: List workers + heartbeat status; useful for fleet visibility. Worth adding for symmetry with cueapi-python #24's same-listed gap.

GET /v1/usage.blocker: Plan, cue count, execution usage, rate limit info. Not yet wrapped.

GET /v1/webhook-secret.blocker: User-account webhook secret retrieval (separate from per-agent webhook). Not yet wrapped.

POST /v1/webhook-secret/regenerate.blocker: Destructive — regenerate the user-account webhook secret. Not yet wrapped; re-evaluate safety.

GET /v1/auth/key.blocker: Inspect current API key metadata. Not yet wrapped — low-value for MCP since the user already has the key (it's how MCP authenticates).

PATCH /v1/auth/me.blocker: Update user profile fields. Not yet wrapped — user-facing settings, more naturally configured via web UI.

GET /v1/alert-webhook-secret.blocker: Alert-webhook secret retrieval. Not yet wrapped.

POST /v1/alert-webhook-secret/regenerate.blocker: Destructive — regenerate alert-webhook secret. Not yet wrapped.

POST /v1/billing/checkout.blocker: Hosted-only — wrap if/when hosted users need programmatic checkout from MCP.

Messaging primitive (all of /v1/agents,.blocker: Phase 12.1.5 messaging primitive is on prod but not yet exposed in MCP. Per current cueapi-core router list: GET/PATCH/DELETE /v1/agents/{ref}, GET /v1/agents/{ref}/webhook-secret, POST /v1/agents/{ref}/webhook-secret/regenerate, GET /v1/agents/{ref}/inbox, GET /v1/agents/{ref}/sent, GET /v1/messages/{msg_id}, POST /v1/messages/{msg_id}/read, POST /v1/messages/{msg_id}/ack. Significant new surface — agent identity, send_message, inbox poll, idempotency-keyed sends, reply threading.
Messaging primitive (all of /v1/agents,.tracking: Major MCP extension. Should land before push delivery (v1.5) goes wide. Same shape as cueapi-python #24's listed gap.

Agent shells (all of /v1/agents/{ref}/sh.blocker: Phase 18 agent-shells API: POST /v1/agents/{ref}/shells (register), GET /v1/agents/{ref}/shells (list), DELETE /v1/agents/{ref}/shells/{shell_id} (deregister), POST /v1/agents/{ref}/shells/{shell_id}/heartbeat (per-shell heartbeat). Distinct from per-execution heartbeat — this is shell-level liveness for the inbox-poll subshell pattern. Not yet wrapped in MCP.

open_implementation_drift.current_impl: Two-step: GET /v1/executions/claimable (discover) + POST /v1/executions/{id}/claim (atomic claim by id).
open_implementation_drift.preferred_impl: Single call to POST /v1/executions/claim (server-side atomic discover+claim).
open_implementation_drift.drift_impact: Race window between discover and claim — another worker could win the same execution between the two HTTP calls. The dedicated /claim route eliminates this. Worth a follow-up PR to migrate.
open_implementation_drift.tracking: Not in Backlog yet; small ergonomic fix — file as separate row when convenient.

covered_response_fields: payload (PR #589 — effective payload, payload_override if set on the fire else parent cue's payload)
missing_response_fields: evidence_external_id, evidence_result_url, evidence_result_type, evidence_summary, evidence_validation_state, evidence_assertions
cueapi_get_execution.tracking: Coverage closed via this PR — tool description updated to surface 'payload' field; passthrough handler already returns it. Remaining response-field gaps (evidence, claim metadata, chain) tracked as separate follow-up.

missing_request_fields: delivery, alerts, catch_up, verification, on_success_fire (cue chaining)
cueapi_create_cue / cueapi_update_cue.tracking: PR #590 fields ported via this PR (require_payload_override + required_payload_keys both schemas + handlers + 7 new tests). Remaining cue-chaining fields tracked as separate follow-up.

cueapi_fire_cue.notes: Today's primary surface for the team-comm payload_override convention. Field coverage is current as of 2026-05-04.

ported_pr_history: Phase 18 Gap 3a (execution-lifecycle endpoints — claim, claim-next, heartbeat, outcome): PORTED — PR #11 (Mike-authored, merged 2026-05-02). Tools cueapi_claim_execution, cueapi_claim_next_execution, cueapi_execution_heartbeat, cueapi_report_outcome.
PR #281 (payload_override on /fire): PORTED — included in PR #11 series via cueapi_fire_cue acceptance of payload_override + merge_strategy.

PR #589 (expose payload on GET /v1/executions): PORTED — this PR (description-only, since the existing get_execution + list_executions tools are passthrough; the new 'payload' field surfaces automatically). cueapi_get_execution and cueapi_list_executions descriptions updated to call out the field.

PR #590 (require_payload_override + required_payload_keys + cue.fire enforcement): PORTED — this PR. Added two new optional fields to cueapi_create_cue + cueapi_update_cue schemas + handler passthroughs. Updated cueapi_fire_cue description to surface the 3 new error codes (payload_override_required, missing_required_payload_keys, inconsistent_message_instruction). 7 new tests cover the new field passthrough and false/empty edge cases.
notes: First seeded 2026-05-04 by CC-cue-mac-app per CTO-PARITY-L2-MCP-ROUTE, mirroring the cueapi-python #24 + cueapi-cli #25 shape. Layer 2 of the 3-layer parity discipline (PR template + this manifest + Backlog rows). Schema may evolve based on what auditors actually need; the `endpoints_missing` and `tool_param_drift` sections are deliberately verbose because they ARE the audit checklist for catching MCP up to the hosted API.
